summary.intent: Resolve automated PR review comments from Copilot and CodeRabbit on PR #392 (E2E test expansion), then fix a CI gap where the release gate was not blocking merges until web E2E tests passed on main.
summary.outcome: All 3 review comments on PR #392 were fixed and resolved (fixture overwrite guard, missing faro_enabled field, page.isClosed() guard). PR #394 was created and merged, introducing a unified ci-e2e.yml orchestrator with path-based change detection and a retrigger mechanism to force the release gate to re-evaluate after post-merge E2E runs. web-e2e job timeout was also raised from 15 to 20 minutes via PR #396.

repo: The release gate (release-gate.yml) previously only enforced E2E checks for release-please branches, auto-passing non-release PRs with 'Not a release PR — E2E gate not applicable'.
E2E tests (web and desktop) ran on push to main but were not required before merging feature PRs; the release gate checked for E2E results only on release-please PRs.
The root cause of the stale gate issue: when a test: commit merged to main, the release-please PR already had a green gate from a prior run — the gate never re-ran to catch the new commit.
desktop-e2e.yml already used dorny/paths-filter for change detection; e2e.yml did not.
Committed fixture files live under tests/web-e2e/fixtures/files/ and must not be overwritten or deleted by test helper functions like createTestMediaFile.
CodeRabbit is subject to per-repo hourly quota limits that can delay reviews by ~20-30 minutes.
The Playwright webServer config uses reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI, meaning in CI it always starts fresh dev servers (API + web), which contributes to E2E run time.

code.finding: createTestMediaFile (and sibling helpers) lacked a guard against overwriting committed fixture files; added a COMMITTED_FIXTURES set check before writing/cleanup.
page.evaluate() in teardown was called without a page.isClosed() guard, risking errors when the page was already closed.
Missing faro_enabled: true metadata field that was expected by the verification step based on the test plan.
dorny/paths-filter requires fetch-depth: 0 to access the before SHA for accurate diff; default fetch-depth: 1 would fail on non-initial pushes.
On branch creation events github.event.before is all zeros; must guard against this before passing to paths-filter.
jq with // empty returns empty string on null, which causes parse errors downstream; use a safer fallback.

workflow: When using gh run rerun to retrigger a release gate, the rerun preserves the original GITHUB_SHA, so any diff-based change detection inside that run (e.g. PREV_TAG..HEAD) uses stale refs — must diff against origin/main instead.

Automated reviewer comments that fall 'outside diff range' are posted as review-level comments, not inline threads, and do not appear in GraphQL reviewThreads; must fetch via gh api repos/.../pulls/.../reviews.
dorny/paths-filter is the established pattern in this repo for conditional job execution based on changed paths.
Reusable workflows (workflow_call) inherit vars context from the calling repo automatically; secrets require secrets: inherit.
Release gate polling MAX_ATTEMPTS must be sized to match the longest possible E2E job timeout (40 attempts * 30s = 20 min to match the 20-min job timeout).

friction: CodeRabbit was rate-limited for ~23 minutes mid-session, requiring extended polling loops before its review arrived.
Polling for new review comments required many manual background bash tasks with sleep intervals due to no native webhook/wait mechanism.
Several gh api REST reply calls timed out and required retries.

The original problem diagnosis went through two wrong hypotheses (release gate not checking feature PRs, then retrigger logic) before identifying the real root cause: stale green checks on the release-please PR after a test: commit landed.
PR #393 was created and immediately closed after the user clarified the actual problem.
dorny/paths-filter emits outside-diff-range comments that cannot be resolved via GraphQL reviewThreads, requiring a separate review-level API call.
open_items: The web-e2e job timeout was raised to 20 minutes, but the underlying slowness (Playwright starting fresh dev servers in CI) has not been addressed — could investigate pre-building or caching server startup.

The retrigger-release-gate job uses gh run rerun which re-runs with stale GITHUB_SHA; the fix (diff against origin/main) was applied to release-gate.yml but the fundamental fragility of rerun-based retriggering vs. a fresh dispatch remains.
